chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ سَعِيدُ بْنُ يَسَارٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ وَهُوَ عَلَى دَابَّتِهِ أَلَهُ أَنْ يُغَطِّيَ وَجْهَهُ وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي قَالَ

translations.en: Saʿīd ibn Yasār asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performs Salat al-Layl while on his mount: may he cover his face while he is praying? He said:

chunks.arabic_text: «أَمَّا إِذَا قَرَأَ فَنَعَمْ وَأَمَّا إِذَا أَوْمَأَ بِوَجْهِهِ لِلسُّجُودِ فَلْيَكْشِفْهُ حَيْثُ مَا أَوْمَأَتْ بِهِ الدَّابَّةُ.

translations.en: "As for when he is reciting, then yes. But as for when he gestures with his face for sajdah, then let him uncover it wherever the mount directs him."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning Salat al-Layl performed while riding an animal during travel. It permits covering the face during recitation, but requires uncovering it when indicating sajdah with the face, showing practical flexibility in supererogatory prayer on a mount.
en.seo_question: Can a person cover his face while performing Salat al-Layl on a riding animal?
